newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga stake in dam cut in new structure.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga stake in dam cut in new structure.

text.p: Malaysia has approved a new equity structure for the operating company of the $5.5 billion Bakun dam, with the stake held by utility firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd cut to five percent from 25, the New Straits Times said on Wednesday.

The equity held by retirement fund Employees Provident Fund in the company, Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd (BHC), will be halved to five percent, the daily quoted Ting Pek Khiing, executive chairman of dam developer Ekran Bhd as saying.
BHEC's other shareholders will retain their equity stakes, with Ekran remaining the largest with a 32 percent stake.
The other shareholders are the Sarawak state government with 19 percent, Sarawak Electricity Supply Corp with nine percent and Malaysian Mining Corp Bhd with five percent.
The dam, in eastern Sarawak state on Borneo island, will have a capacity of 2,400 megawatts.

Ting told reporters in Sarawak the government has approved the listing of BHC on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, with local public investors alloted 15 percent of its shares and the remaining 10 percent for foreign investors.

"We will be making efforts to do this (the listing) by the end of this year," Ting was quoted as saying. BHC is expected to float at least two billion shares at around 1.80 ringgit ($0.72) each in the initial public offering.
